title: Private Console Smart Summary Cards and Actionable Toggles
creator: Imani Chen
description:
Problem: Operators using Private/VPC deployments need a concise, action-first surface that summarizes cluster network health, upgrade state, and cost trends without diving into multiple pages. Current status pages and cost breakdowns require too many clicks and separate dashboards for alerts, egress/cost spikes, and rolling upgrades.

Goals:
- Surface a single-row "smart summary" for each cluster that combines: network reachability status, recent packet-drop or NAT errors, upgrade progress, and a 7-day cost sparkline.
- Provide inline actionable toggles (e.g., enable/disable egress-cache, toggle rolling upgrade pause, open quick rollback) that run guarded flows via Console operations APIs.
- Keep the surface compact so operators can scan dozens of clusters. Allow expansion to a 2-column detail pane for deeper logs and per-tenant cost breakdowns.
- Ensure accessibility, keyboard-first interactions, and clear failure states for unsafe actions.

Proposed solution:
1) Smart Summary Card (compact list row): leftmost cluster identity, status pill (green/amber/red) with micro-copy, a 7-day sparkline for cost (hover reveals day values), small icons for recent incidents and upgrade state (hover/cards show summary).
2) Network Lens CTA: a single click opens an overlay with an interactive topology snapshot (static image in prototype) and quick links to traceroute, connectivity test, and open support ticket.
3) Actionable Toggles and Buttons: inline toggles for: "Pause Upgrades", "Egress Cache" and a contextual primary button that morphs ("Resume Upgrade", "Rollback to vX", "Investigate"), guarded by confirmation and role check (RBAC).
4) Expansion panel: when a row is expanded, show two columns - left: timeline of recent health events, recent PR/upgrade links, logs snapshot; right: cost breakdown (egress, storage, GPU hours) and tenant-level contributors, with a one-click link to create a cost alert.
5) Safety: destructive actions routed through the existing operations API with explicit confirmation modals and optional staged canary windows.

Prototype status: Figma prototype created (link below). Interactive prototype covers the compact list, expansion behavior, and the confirmation flows for toggles. Engineering notes included for animation timings and data loading states.

Success metrics:
- Reduction in mean time to first action on incidents for Private clusters by 25% (tracked via Console click telemetry).
- 30% fewer page navigations per incident investigation (operators complete actions from the smart summary).
- No increase in unsafe rollbacks after 30 days (safety checks validated in audit logs).
acceptance_criteria: Compact card renders at 48px height in dense mode and 64px in regular mode with all elements legible
Inline toggles trigger the expected Console operations API calls and show optimistic state
Expansion pane shows topology snapshot and cost breakdown within 300ms of open on 95th percentile connections
All primary actions require RBAC validation and explicit confirmation modal with reason input for audits
Keyboard tab order and ARIA labels present for all interactive elements
Prototype reviewed and signed off by eng and PM with a follow-up implementation plan
design_notes: Use compact sparkline treatment borrowed from cost dashboard but remove axis labels to save vertical space; value appears on hover
Status pill contains semantic short form copy: OK / Degraded / Partitioned; we avoid 'Failed' to reduce panic
Actionable toggles are contextual: disabled if last incident < 15m ago unless operator has override permission
We show 'last successful health check' timestamp as subordinate text to give recency context
Prototype includes a reduced-motion variant and color-contrast tweaks for the amber state

All action responses must include trace id and be forwarded to audit-log service
